exercises.name: Waiter Curl (Dumbbell)

source_english.description: Waiter Curl (Dumbbell) curls both dumbbells from a palms-forward standing position while the elbows stay close to the body.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold one dumbbell in each hand with palms facing forward.
Keep the upper arms beside the ribs and curl both dumbbells toward the shoulders.
Pause at the top without lifting the elbows.
Lower the dumbbells slowly until the elbows are nearly straight.
source_english.safety_note: Use dumbbells you can lower without leaning or swinging.

source_english.description: A Back Extension (Machine) uses a supported hip hinge: the torso lowers from the hips and returns only to a neutral line.
instructions: Set the machine so the hips are supported and the feet or legs are secured.
Hinge forward from the hips with a neutral spine and keep the head aligned.
Raise the torso until it is in line with the legs by squeezing the glutes.
Pause briefly, then lower under control without rounding deeply.
common_mistakes: Using the arms to create momentum.
source_english.safety_note: Stop at a neutral torso line; do not force the machine or bench into hyperextension.

instructions: Secure the belt of the machine around the hips and stand on the platform with a stable stance.

Descend to a comfortable depth while keeping the feet planted.
Drive through the platform to stand without locking the knees aggressively.
form_cues: Keep the torso supported by the belt.
source_english.safety_note: Check the belt and platform connection before loading the machine.

source_english.description: A machine rear kick extends one hip backward against a pad or lever while the torso stays square.
instructions: Adjust the machine pad and foot or ankle lever for your height.
Brace your hands and torso against the supports and place one leg on the lever.
Drive that leg straight back by extending the hip without arching the spine.
Pause at the end, then return the leg slowly and switch sides.
source_english.safety_note: Set the machine stop and use a load that keeps the pelvis supported.
